entries.subject: Visible and near-infrared albedo
entries.finding: The selected Golish/USGS maps provide 550 and 950 nm normalized MSI albedo views. The retained 550 nm native label was inspected: 10682×5341 float samples, FilterNumber 1, Center 550 nm, and Equirectangular, planetocentric, east-positive 0–360° mapping centered at 180°. The filename contains sinu, but the label declares the selected projection. Its 17 km cartographic reference radius and 10 m/pixel sampling are not the body’s physical radius or guaranteed terrain resolution. The two bands remain separate, not a mineral-abundance ratio.

entries.subject: Shape and Elevation
entries.finding: [Gaskell ver128q](https://sbnarchive.psi.edu/pds4/non_mission/gaskell.ast-eros.shape-model/data/vertex/ver128q.tab), 196,608 released facets. Elevation is radius minus 8.42 km, not gravitational height.

entries.subject: Named features
entries.finding: [IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Page/EROS/target) Eros centre-point export, snapshot 2026-09-11, public domain. IAU-adopted names with centre, diameter, extent and name origin; labels appear at the closest zoom only, and a selected feature stays labelled.

entries.subject: Native SBMT preparation comparison
entries.finding: The generic native SBMT oracle compares the full released mesh, the MSI FITS exposure and both corrected SUM and SPICE INFO camera cases. Sampled pointing, image values and visible intersections match. Maximum in-image UV difference across the tested orientations/crop is 0.0817 pixel, within the fixed 0.25-pixel criterion. This is preparation test evidence, not qualification of a new surface dataset.

entries.subject: All seven MSI wavelength maps
entries.finding: The five remaining Golish 2023 MSI maps at 450, 760, 900, 1000 and 1050 nm join the existing 550 and 950 nm maps in one Reflected light group. All seven retain the common 0.05–0.40 I/F display range, Gaskell shape and original cartographic frame. The 1000 nm XML repeats the 550 nm logical identifier; its filename and ISIS filter label identify the correct member, so the catalogue records that archive member. Independent native-byte probes pass. Existing 550/950 nm links, installed assets and all seven browser selections were checked.

entries.subject: Roberts Eros Ponds Catalog V1.1 as the Ponds dataset
entries.finding: The PDS SBN bundle urn:nasa:pds:ast-eros.roberts.ponds-catalog::1.1 (doi:10.26033/4dqc-8067) lists 334 ponds with IAU_EROS centres in km, planetocentric latitude and east longitude, radial distance and one characteristic diameter each (7.4 to 213.6 m, median 49.9 m), identified by P. C. Thomas and relocated on the Gaskell SPC shape with SBMT. Because it publishes diameters, each pond is drawn as the set of source-surface points within half its diameter of the centre, not as a one-cell presence mark. Every row's Cartesian centre reproduces its printed latitude, longitude and distance within 0.009° and 1.1 m. Projected onto ver128q, 326 centres lie within 27.4 m of the surface (median 2.3 m, 95th percentile 12.6 m); 8 lie 66 to 384 m away (ponds 1, 2, 10, 129, 216, 218, 219, 255) and are withheld by the 60 m limit chosen beforehand, a little under half the 131.9 m median ver128q edge; three of them (1, 2, 255) miss it by only 6 to 9 m. The SBMT copy of the table matches the CSV to 0.5 m and carries the cyan colour 0,255,255 the dataset uses.

entries.subject: Ponds as labelled surface features
entries.finding: The catalogue names ponds only by number (Pond001 to Pond334) and the surface-features bank is built for IAU names with search and captions. 334 numbered labels would add no names; the categorical dataset carries position and size instead.
entries.revisitWhen: The IAU names individual ponds, or the catalogue adds the polygon or ellipse outlines its caveats promise.

entries.subject: NEAR X-ray and gamma-ray element maps
entries.finding: SBN archives only XGRS spectra (NEAR_A_XRS_2/3_EDR and NEAR_A_GRS_2/3_EDR data sets, cruise, orbit and surface phases); no derived abundance product exists in the archive. The published results are an eight-flare XRS average that Lim and Nittler (2009) say probably represents the whole of Eros and cannot establish or rule out spatial variation, and gamma-ray values measured only at the landing site (Evans et al. 2001; Peplowski et al. 2015). Neither supports a map, so the values are factsheet facts cited to the papers' tables.
entries.revisitWhen: A derived, spatially resolved abundance product for Eros is archived.

entries.subject: NEAR X-ray and gamma-ray composition facts
entries.finding: Six facts: X-ray Mg/Si, Fe/Si and S/Si from Lim and Nittler (2009) Table 9, uncorrected eight-flare averages, which supersede the Nittler et al. (2001) calibration; landing-site Fe/Si by mass (1.19 ± 0.30, 2 SD) and hydrogen (1,100 ppm, 400 to 2,700 ppm) from Peplowski et al. (2015) Table 2 and abstract; landing-site potassium 0.07% with the 40% uncertainty Evans et al. (2001) assign to all their gamma-ray results. The extracts, locators and uncertainty meanings are in source/editorial/factsheet-review.json.

entries.subject: Global gamma-ray composition from the orbital data (Peplowski 2016)
entries.finding: Peplowski (2016), Planetary and Space Science 134, 36-51, reports the first gamma-ray signal from orbit, from about 10 hours of low-altitude flyovers, with global Fe and Th concentrations and a global K concentration (abstract). The article is open access (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) but the publisher and mirror downloads returned HTTP 403 or 404 on 2026-09-28, so its values were not read and no fact uses them.
entries.revisitWhen: The full text is read; its global Fe, Th and K values would join the factsheet as whole-body facts.

entries.subject: The NEAR landing site in the ponds catalogue
entries.finding: Peplowski et al. (2015) describe the landing site as a ponded deposit (after Veverka et al. 2001), but the nearest catalogued pond (334, 16.7 m) lies about 5.5° of arc, roughly 0.6 km, from the landing coordinates in source/features/sites.json. The site coordinates are the 2001 solution, which Barnouin et al. (2012) later revised; the frames were not compared.
entries.revisitWhen: The revised landing coordinates are placed in the IAU_EROS frame of the catalogue.

entries.subject: Ponds drawn over the 550 nm photograph
entries.finding: The first Ponds bake drew non-pond ground as a flat grey category, so the 1 to 2 pixel ponds read as an empty body. The dataset now has one category and leaves non-pond surface missing; the missing texels show the 550 nm photograph in grey at 35% brightness and 6 bits, the catalogue-dataset rule used on Mars and Phobos. On the body the photograph is sampled exactly as the 550 nm view's native atlas samples it (same leaf transform and 2 × 2 texel footprint on the original Golish map), so both views share one texel grid. Contrast: the cyan pond colour differs from every dimmed photograph value by at least 47.1 OKLab units (5th percentile 64.7, median 69.6) over 14,252,095 samples, every fourth native value of the 550 nm map.
